lead.headline: Cherry Blossom was down 60.2. It won by 26.84.
lead.dek: Bad things man bad things led by 60.2 at 1:07 p.m. Sunday, then froze at 136.16 for the rest of the afternoon. Jonah Coleman’s touchdown at 4:02 p.m. flipped it, and the No. 2 team in the league lost 181.4 to 154.56.
lead.pull: Up 60.2 at 1:07 p.m. Behind for good at 4:02 p.m.
body: At 1:07 p.m. Sunday, Bad things man bad things led Cherry Blossom by 60.2. C.J. Stroud had banked 21.46 on Thursday night. Chuba Hubbard and Tetairoa McMillan had turned one early game into a 45.1-point stack. The No. 2 team in the league had a lead you could see from orbit. I’ve covered Cherry Blossom all season. At 1:07 p.m. I was drafting the obituary.

Then the afternoon happened, and only one team showed up for it. Bad things man bad things’ total stopped at 136.16 and stayed there until Sunday night. Cherry Blossom kept coming. Parker Washington and Trevor Lawrence put up 33.04 together. Jonah Coleman scored 34.9, and he isn’t a fluke: his opportunities are up from 10.0 to 25.0 a game over the last two weeks, with an 81% snap share. That isn’t a hot hand. That’s a job.

At 4:02 p.m., Coleman went 7 yards for a touchdown and Cherry Blossom led 138.72 to 136.16. It never trailed again. It finished Sunday up 169.1 to 144.56, Tee Higgins caught a 31-yard touchdown at 6:22 p.m. Monday, and the lead peaked at 33.84 at 8:04 p.m. Final: 181.4 to 154.56. Travis Kelce added 25.4 with two touchdowns, Jameson Williams 19.3 with a 57-yard score at 11:50 a.m., and Cherry Blossom left only 2.1 on its bench.

Bad things man bad things had chances to make this closer and none to win it. On Wednesday at 12:11 a.m. it claimed Jordyn Tyson and dropped Ladd McConkey. Tyson started and scored 2.0. McConkey, still on the wire, scored 20.7. Kirk Cousins started at quarterback for 8.4 while Tyler Shough scored 15.28 on the bench. Fix both and it still loses. That’s what a 60.2-point collapse looks like: there isn’t even one guy to blame.

Cherry Blossom is 6-5, second in the league in points with 1856.56, and its playoff odds are 100%. It has made 5 moves all season, the fewest in the league, and it just took down a team that has made 30. Bad things man bad things is 8-3, a game behind Poochinski, and still has an 84.8% shot at a top-two seed. It also has a lesson: a lead at 1:07 p.m. is a rumor, not a result.

games.headline: Poochinski hangs 199.64 on Santa Clara’s Finest
games.dek: The Dallas stack scored 100.2 by itself. The lead hit 123.16 at 1:00 p.m. Sunday. Final margin: 92.38, the biggest of the week.
body: Santa Clara’s Finest led this game from Thursday night until Sunday morning. The Houston Texans D/ST scored 15.0 on Thursday night and the Finest went to bed up 16.0. Then at 10:14 a.m. Sunday, Javonte Williams scored from 1 yard out and Poochinski never looked back.

Poochinski’s Dallas stack did the rest: Dak Prescott 35.9, CeeDee Lamb 30.2, Javonte Williams 24.1 and Brandon Aubrey 10.0. That’s 100.2 from one stack. Jahmyr Gibbs scored twice in the fourth quarter of the early window and finished with 27.8. At 1:00 p.m. Poochinski led 175.24 to 52.08.

And then, with the game long decided, the front office kept working. At 12:51 p.m. Sunday it added the San Francisco 49ers D/ST for Tyler Higbee and started it. It scored 16.0. Against a team called Santa Clara’s Finest. The only blemish: Aaron Rodgers, dropped at 9:23 a.m. for Kaelon Black, scored 15.98 for nobody. Final: 199.64 to 107.26. Poochinski is 9-2 with a perfect lineup and the week’s high score.

games.headline: The champ cuts Drake Maye and wins anyway
games.dek: Maye I touch your TDs? swapped its namesake for Cam Ward on Wednesday. Ward scored 22.22, the lineup was perfect, and the playoff odds jumped to 70.8%.
body: Big Stric Energy started fast. Nico Collins caught a 42-yard touchdown at 5:49 p.m. Thursday, and at 10:24 a.m. Sunday Big Stric led 32.04 to 11.7, a 20.34-point cushion. That was the high-water mark.

At 11:38 a.m., Zay Flowers caught a 25-yard pass and Maye I touch your TDs? took the lead, 51.3 to 49.32. Six minutes later Cam Ward ran one in. At 12:00 p.m. Ward threw a 59-yard touchdown. At 12:06 p.m. Bucky Irving scored. By 1:36 p.m. the champ led by 44.08. Emmett Johnson scored 24.3, Ward 22.22, Brock Purdy 22.2. Maye left 0.0 on its bench. Final: 163.52 to 140.4.

Big Stric Energy got 27.9 from Ashton Jeanty and 17.0 from Tyler Bass, and started Dalton Kincaid, who didn’t play, at tight end for 0.0. The best lineup it could have set scored 145.2, still short. It’s 2-9, on a three-game losing streak, and its playoff odds are 3.5%.

games.headline: deeboliciouskins never trails, wins by 72.88
games.dek: deeboliciouskins led from Jonathan Taylor’s first carry Thursday night to the final whistle Monday. AB81 never led for a single second.
body: Jonathan Taylor ran for 6 yards at 5:20 p.m. Thursday and deeboliciouskins took a lead it never gave up. AB81’s biggest lead all week: 0. Not a typo. Four of its starters were on bye, and you can read about that below in a section this desk wishes it didn’t need.

deeboliciouskins did its part. Patrick Mahomes scored 24.96, George Pickens 23.8 and Malik Nabers 18.5. Drew Stevens, added at 9:42 a.m. Sunday for Kyler Murray, kicked his way to 18.0 Monday night. Entering Monday it led 108.06 to 75.34, and the lead peaked at 75.88 at 8:17 p.m. Monday. Final: 151.22 to 78.34.

Not everything was tidy. DJ Moore scored 23.1 on the bench while Jonathan Taylor started and scored 6.7, and T.J. Hockenson’s 11.5 sat behind Tyler Warren’s 3.2. That’s 24.7 left on the bench, the most of any winner. Against this opponent it didn’t matter. deeboliciouskins is 6-5 with a two-game win streak and 100% playoff odds.

beats.headline: Led by 20.34, then the champ woke up
body: Big Stric Energy led by 20.34 at 10:24 a.m. Sunday and lost by 23.12. Nico Collins’ Thursday touchdown, Ashton Jeanty’s 27.9 and Tyler Bass’s 17.0 kept this team in it for exactly one morning.

The lineup had one hole that nobody could fix: Dalton Kincaid started at tight end, didn’t play, and scored 0.0. Tucker Kraft scored 0.0 on the bench too, so there was no answer on the roster. Saquon Barkley’s 13.5 on the bench over Jalen Coker’s 8.7 is the only swap, worth 4.8. The best lineup scored 145.2 and still loses.
2-9, eighth in the standings, three straight losses, and playoff odds of 3.5%. The all-play record is 25-52. This team isn’t unlucky. It’s just losing.
beats.insight: Tucker Kraft is in the projected lineup at tight end (10.77); start him and leave Kincaid on the bench until he plays. Barkley (13.73 projected) belongs in the lineup over Coker at flex. Big Stric Energy projects for 154.19 and is a 52.7% favorite over AB81, the closest thing to a must-win a 3.5% team can have.

beats.headline: Nine wins, 199.64, and a 49ers joke
body: Poochinski scored 199.64, the week’s high, with a perfect lineup: 0.0 left on the bench. The Dallas stack produced 100.2, and Jahmyr Gibbs added 27.8. This is what the best team in the league looks like when everything works.

The front office even found time for comedy. It added the San Francisco 49ers D/ST at 12:51 p.m. Sunday, started it against Santa Clara’s Finest, and got 16.0. The one miss: it dropped Aaron Rodgers at 9:23 a.m. Sunday, and Rodgers scored 15.98 on the wire.
9-2, first in points with 1906.56, a three-game win streak, an all-play record of 54-23 and a 99.5% chance at a top-two seed.
beats.insight: Poochinski now rosters only two quarterbacks in a two-QB league, so one injury means an empty slot. Grab a backup: J.J. McCarthy projects for 17.64 and Aaron Rodgers, the one it just cut, for 14.2. Poochinski projects for 180.94 and is a 66.7% favorite over deeboliciouskins.

beats.headline: Cut Maye, kept the season alive
body: Maye I touch your TDs? dropped Drake Maye, its own second-round pick and the inspiration for its name, on Wednesday at 12:11 a.m. and claimed Cam Ward. Ward scored 22.22, the best pickup of the week. Sentiment is a luxury. Wins aren’t.

The lineup was perfect, 163.52 with 0.0 on the bench, after three straight weeks of the bench deciding games. Emmett Johnson scored 24.3, Purdy 22.2, Zay Flowers 16.4 with the 25-yard catch that took the lead for good at 11:38 a.m.
3-8, but the playoff odds jumped to 70.8%, the best of the three teams chasing the last spot. The luck rating is -2.1, the worst in the league. The champ is still owed.
beats.insight: Start Emmett Johnson every week. The projection (6.5) hasn’t caught up: his opportunities are up from 5.2 to 28.0 a game, his snap share from 27% to 85%, and he’s averaging 29.7 over the last two. Put him in for Christian Watson or Drake London. Maye projects for 154.71 against Cherry Blossom and is a 43.6% underdog.

beats.headline: Down 60.2, won by 26.84
body: I wrote the lead, so I’ll keep this short: Cherry Blossom trailed by 60.2 at 1:07 p.m. Sunday and won by 26.84. Jonah Coleman scored 34.9, Kelce 25.4, and the lineup left only 2.1 on the bench.

This franchise has made 5 moves all season, the fewest in the league. It doesn’t tinker. It sets the lineup and lets its players work, and this week they worked the whole afternoon while Bad things man bad things sat on 136.16.
6-5, second in points, 100% playoff odds, and an 8.1% shot at a top-two seed. The all-play record is 45-32.
beats.insight: Jaylen Warren is losing his job: opportunities down from 19.4 to 12.5 a game and snap share from 72% to 53%, and he scored 4.9 at flex this week. He still sits in the projected flex (14.02); consider Tre Tucker, who outscored him from the bench. Cherry Blossom projects for 161.37 and is a 56.3% favorite over Maye I touch your TDs?.

beats.headline: A 60.2-point lead, and then nothing
body: Bad things man bad things led by 60.2 at 1:07 p.m. Sunday. Its total froze at 136.16 until Sunday night, and it lost 181.4 to 154.56. Chuba Hubbard (26.0) and Tetairoa McMillan (19.1) did their jobs early. Nobody did anything late.

Two decisions hurt. Wednesday’s waiver swap of Ladd McConkey for Jordyn Tyson turned into 20.7 on the wire and 2.0 in the lineup. Kirk Cousins started over Tyler Shough, 8.4 to 15.28. Neither cost the game, which is the only good news here.
8-3, second in the standings, an all-play of 50-27 and an 84.8% chance at a top-two seed. Thirty moves this season, the most in the league. This week, two of them backfired.
beats.insight: The quarterback call is the one to get right: Cousins projects for 17.92 in the second QB slot, but he scored 8.4 this week while Shough scored 15.28 on the bench. Check the matchups before kickoff. Bad things man bad things projects for 160.54 against Santa Clara’s Finest at 160.53, dead even at 50%, the closest game on the board.

beats.headline: Never trailed, still left 24.7 behind
body: deeboliciouskins led from 5:20 p.m. Thursday to the end and won by 72.88. Mahomes scored 24.96, Pickens 23.8, Nabers 18.5, and Sunday-morning pickup Drew Stevens kicked 18.0 Monday night.

But DJ Moore is a running bit now. He scored 23.1 on the bench while Jonathan Taylor scored 6.7 in the lineup. A week ago Moore scored 19.4 on the bench. The week before that, 6.6. Somebody start the man.
6-5, a two-game win streak, 100% playoff odds, and Marcus Mariota added 4 times, the league’s most-repeated pickup. Old habits.
beats.insight: Ride George Pickens: his target share over the last two weeks is 34% and he’s averaging 33.65 in that span; the projected flex spot (13.69) undersells him. Watch D’Andre Swift, whose opportunities are down from 21.5 to 14.0 a game with 40% of his points from touchdowns. Only two QBs on the roster after dropping Kyler Murray; a backup is cheap insurance. deeboliciouskins projects for 162.78 and is a 33.3% underdog to Poochinski.

beats.headline: Led into Sunday, lost by 92.38
body: Santa Clara’s Finest led Poochinski 16.0 to 0.0 after Thursday night, thanks to the Houston Texans D/ST. It held the lead until 10:14 a.m. Sunday. Then it lost by 92.38, the biggest margin of the week.

The front office was busy, as usual. On Wednesday at 12:11 a.m. it re-claimed Lamar Jackson, the quarterback it cut a week earlier, and benched him for 0.0. Early Saturday it made three moves between 4:29 a.m. and 4:31 a.m., adding Rome Odunze (8.5) and Ryan Flournoy and dropping Jeremiyah Love. It started Bryce Young (16.96) over Baker Mayfield (19.08). Five late-night moves this season, the most in the league.
3-8, and the playoff odds fell from 57.1% to 25.7% in one week. The 107.26 is this team’s lowest score of the season.
beats.insight: Set the quarterbacks as projected: Joe Burrow (24.23) and Mayfield (15.39), not Young. Cam Skattebo is the engine, with snap share up to 87% and a 19.7 projection. Santa Clara’s Finest projects for 160.53 against Bad things man bad things at 160.54, a 50% coin flip that probably decides whether this team plays in December.

beats.headline: Four byes, four zeros, never led
body: AB81 started Matthew Stafford, Kyren Williams, Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Rhamondre Stevenson. All four were on bye. Four zeros. The team scored 78.34, the week’s low, and never led for a second.

Mike Evans (22.9), George Kittle (18.4) and DeVonta Smith (9.1) sat on the bench. The best lineup scored 128.74, which still loses to 151.22, so this was a loss either way. That doesn’t make it less absurd.

7-4, third in the standings, three straight losses. The all-play record is 30-47, and the luck rating is 2.7, the highest in the league. The playoff odds are still 100%, which tells you more about the schedule than the team.
beats.insight: The byes are over and the projected lineup is full: Smith-Njigba (24.62) is back, Evans (13.71) slides to flex and Kittle (12.24) to tight end. Set it before Thursday. Derrick Henry gets 40% of his points from touchdowns, so expect swings. AB81 projects for 151.34 and is a 47.3% underdog to Big Stric Energy.

smart_move.stat_label: Cam Ward, claimed Wednesday at 12:11 a.m.
smart_move.headline: Maye I touch your TDs? cut its namesake
smart_move.dek: Drake Maye out, Cam Ward in. Ward scored 22.22, the best pickup of the week, and the champ’s playoff odds jumped to 70.8%.
body: Drake Maye was this franchise’s second-round pick. He is also, if you read the team name, the whole brand. On Wednesday at 12:11 a.m., Maye I touch your TDs? dropped him and claimed Cam Ward.

Ward ran for a touchdown at 11:44 a.m. Sunday and threw a 59-yard touchdown at 12:00 p.m., right as the champ was turning a 1.98-point lead into a 44.08-point one. He finished with 22.22, the best pickup started by anyone this week. The same front office also grabbed the Buffalo Bills D/ST on Wednesday at 11:48 a.m. and got 8.0.
The champ won 163.52 to 140.4 with a perfect lineup, and its playoff odds went from 25.2% to 70.8%. A name is forever. A roster spot is week to week.

dumb_move.headline: AB81 started four players on bye
dumb_move.dek: Stafford, Kyren Williams, Smith-Njigba and Stevenson. Four zeros. Mike Evans (22.9) and George Kittle (18.4) watched from the bench.
body: Last week’s edition warned that AB81 had five starters on bye. Four of them stayed in the lineup: Matthew Stafford at quarterback, Kyren Williams at running back, Jaxon Smith-Njigba at receiver and Rhamondre Stevenson at flex. Each scored 0.0.

The bench had answers for three of them. Mike Evans scored 22.9 on the bench. George Kittle scored 18.4. DeVonta Smith scored 9.1. That’s 50.4 points left on the bench, the most in the league by double. With Evans and Kittle in, AB81 enters Monday ahead of deeboliciouskins instead of down 108.06 to 75.34. The bench quarterbacks, Sam Darnold and Jalen Hurts, scored 0.0 too, so the Stafford slot needed a waiver add that never came.

Did it cost the game? No. The best lineup scored 128.74 and deeboliciouskins scored 151.22. But this is the third straight loss for a 7-4 team with a 30-47 all-play record and the league’s luckiest rating. Luck can cover a lot. It can’t cover four empty chairs.

bench_beat.stat_label: Points left on the bench in a win
bench_beat.headline: DJ Moore, bench star, again
bench_beat.dek: DJ Moore scored 23.1 on the bench while Jonathan Taylor started for 6.7. It’s the third straight week Moore has outscored a starter from the bench.
body: deeboliciouskins started Jonathan Taylor. He scored 6.7. DJ Moore sat on the bench and scored 23.1. Swap them and that’s 16.4 points. Start T.J. Hockenson (11.5) instead of Tyler Warren (3.2) and that’s 8.3 more. The best lineup scored 175.92.

None of that mattered against AB81, which scored 78.34. deeboliciouskins won by 72.88. But this is a pattern: Moore scored 19.4 on the bench in Week 10 and 6.6 on the bench in Week 9. In Week 9, this team lost by 22.4.
The playoffs start in Week 15, and there are no AB81s with four byes in the bracket. Somewhere in this lineup is a spot for Moore.

swing_plays.headline: Jonah Coleman finishes the comeback
swing_plays.blurb: Coleman’s 7-yard touchdown at 4:02 p.m. Sunday put Cherry Blossom ahead 138.72 to 136.16, three hours after it trailed by 60.2. It never trailed again.

swing_plays.blurb: A 57-yard touchdown from Jared Goff at 11:50 a.m. was worth 18.98 to Cherry Blossom, cutting a 69.26 to 48.64 deficit to 69.26 to 67.62. The lead would grow again before the afternoon flipped it.

swing_plays.blurb: A 25-yard catch at 11:38 a.m. Sunday put Maye I touch your TDs? ahead of Big Stric Energy 51.3 to 49.32. The lead grew to 44.08 by 1:36 p.m.

swing_plays.headline: Nico Collins’ Thursday touchdown
swing_plays.blurb: Big Stric Energy’s 42-yard touchdown at 5:49 p.m. Thursday was worth 11.2 and started a lead that lasted until Sunday morning. It peaked at 20.34.

swing_plays.blurb: Prescott’s 8-yard touchdown to CeeDee Lamb at 10:49 a.m. was a 12.12-point stack play, pushing Poochinski to 61.32 against 30.58. The lead reached 123.16 by 1:00 p.m.

features.headline: Deadline week came and went. Still zero trades.
features.dek: Week 11 was the R.A.T.S. trade deadline. Three teams are fighting for one playoff spot, three teams run with two quarterbacks, and nobody called anybody.
body: Week 11 was the trade deadline in R.A.T.S. The all-time trade count is 0. It was 0 last week, it was 0 last season, and I am told it will be 0 when the sun burns out.

This was the week for it. Maye I touch your TDs?, Santa Clara’s Finest and Big Stric Energy are fighting for one playoff spot. Poochinski, Maye and deeboliciouskins each roster only two quarterbacks in a two-QB league. AB81 had Mike Evans, George Kittle and DeVonta Smith on its bench while four empty slots started. Supply, demand, a deadline. Nothing.
So the rest of the season gets decided on the waiver wire, where 11 moves happened this week and the best-performing ones were the ones nobody made: Fernando Mendoza scored 23.88 unrostered.

features.headline: The best receivers this week were free agents
features.dek: Bad things man bad things cut Ladd McConkey for Jordyn Tyson. McConkey scored 20.7 on the wire. Tyson scored 2.0 in the lineup.
body: At 12:11 a.m. Wednesday, Bad things man bad things claimed Jordyn Tyson and dropped Ladd McConkey. Tyson started and scored 2.0. McConkey scored 20.7 for nobody, the fifth-best unrostered score in the league.
He had company. Fernando Mendoza scored 23.88, Jack Bech 22.8, Ted Hurst III 22.6 and Antonio Williams 21.2, all unrostered. Aaron Rodgers, dropped by Poochinski at 9:23 a.m. Sunday, scored 15.98.

Not every move missed. Cam Ward scored 22.22 for Maye I touch your TDs?, Drew Stevens 18.0 for deeboliciouskins and the San Francisco 49ers D/ST 16.0 for Poochinski. The lesson of Week 11: the wire is deep, and you have to actually start the right guy.

busted.headline: AB81 starts four byes; Big Stric starts a tight end who sat
busted.blurb: AB81 started Matthew Stafford, Kyren Williams, Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Rhamondre Stevenson, all on bye, for four zeros. w12-m3.headline: Poochinski is a 66.7% favorite over deeboliciouskins
w12-m3.blurb: Poochinski projects for 180.94 to deeboliciouskins’ 162.78 and is a 66.7% favorite. Both rosters carry only two quarterbacks. deeboliciouskins’ best shot is starting DJ Moore and riding George Pickens.

w12-m2.headline: The champ’s playoff push meets Cherry Blossom
w12-m2.blurb: Cherry Blossom projects for 161.37 to Maye I touch your TDs?’ 154.71 and is a 56.3% favorite. Maye is at 70.8% for the last playoff spot; a win here nearly locks it. Watch Emmett Johnson against Jonah Coleman, the two fastest-rising backs in the league.

w12-m4.headline: Coin flip with the last playoff spot on it
w12-m4.blurb: Bad things man bad things projects for 160.54, Santa Clara’s Finest for 160.53. Spread: 0.01. Win odds: 50% to 50%. The Finest are at 25.7% for the playoffs and need this one; Bad things man bad things needs it to hold off Cherry Blossom for a top-two seed.

playoff_note: Three weeks left, six playoff spots. Poochinski, Bad things man bad things, Cherry Blossom, deeboliciouskins and AB81 are all at 100% in the simulations. The top-two race: Poochinski 99.5%, Bad things man bad things 84.8%, Cherry Blossom 8.1%, AB81 4.5%, deeboliciouskins 3.1%. The last spot flipped again: Maye I touch your TDs? jumped from 25.2% to 70.8%, Santa Clara’s Finest fell from 57.1% to 25.7%, and Big Stric Energy dropped from 17.7% to 3.5%. Next week Maye plays Cherry Blossom, the Finest play Bad things man bad things in a 50% to 50% coin flip, and Big Stric plays AB81.
